summary: Feed s174_triple is degraded: 8.9% duplicate packets, 100% missing VLAN tags for required VLANs 10,20, and 8.6% TCP packet loss. IDS requires full payload and both directions, so incomplete streams and missing segmentation severely reduce detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags or SPAN configured as access/untagged - 100% of packets arrive untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are never seen.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot enforce VLAN-aware policies for VLANs 10,20; all traffic appears flat, causing missed lateral movement, incorrect asset attribution, and blind spots for segment-specific detections.

recommended_fix.why: Enable VLAN tag preservation on broker ingress/egress and explicitly forward VLANs 10,20 to this IDS feed so tags are delivered intact.

findings.root_cause: SPAN mirror buffer overflow or packet broker oversubscription dropping packets before the IDS - 201 of 2333 TCP packets (8.6%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating loss in the visibility path, not at the endpoint.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS receives incomplete TCP streams with missing segments; with needs_full_payload=true, stream reassembly and signature matching fail and attacks split across missing packets will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN with passive TAP and ensure broker capacity/buffering is sufficient to deliver complete, lossless streams to the 1Gbps IDS port.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice - likely both sides of a TAP aggregated or two SPAN sessions feeding the same broker port without deduplication, resulting in 219 of 2453 packets (8.9%) duplicates.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles re-analyzing duplicates, inflates flow/event counts, and can mis-handle TCP reassembly/state tracking, reducing effective detection capacity.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication on this feed to suppress identical packets within a short time window before delivery to IDS.
